title: The Taylor Series of cos/sin from the Exponential Definition
description: The parent chain (euler-identity) proves Euler's formula e^{ix} = cos x + i·sin x and e^{iπ} = −1. Its OQ-01-OQ-02 asks to derive cos_eq_tsum (the power series of cos) from the Mathlib definition cos z = (e^{iz} + e^{−iz})/2. In Mathlib Complex.cos is defined via exponentials, and its power series cos z = Σ (−1)ⁿ z²ⁿ/(2n)! is derived from that definition. This entry packages the exponential form, the power series of cos/sin (over ℂ and ℝ), Euler's formula, and Euler's identity — the chain definition → series → identity. 0 axioms.

overview.historicalContext: Euler's formula e^{ix} = cos x + i·sin x ties the complex exponential to the trigonometric functions, and at x = π yields Euler's identity e^{iπ} = −1, often called the most beautiful equation in mathematics. There are two natural ways to set up the theory. One defines cos and sin by their power series cos z = Σ (−1)ⁿ z²ⁿ/(2n)!, sin z = Σ (−1)ⁿ z²ⁿ⁺¹/(2n+1)! and derives Euler's formula. The other — Mathlib's choice — defines them through the exponential, cos z = (e^{iz} + e^{−iz})/2 and sin z = (e^{−iz} − e^{iz})·i/2, and then proves the power series as theorems. The parent gallery entry proves Euler's formula and identity; its OQ-01-OQ-02 asks to derive the power series of cos from the exponential definition, which Mathlib provides via Complex.cos_eq_tsum. This entry packages the full chain definition → series → identity.
overview.problemStatement: Derive the Taylor (power) series of cos from the exponential definition cos z = (e^{iz} + e^{−iz})/2, and record the companion facts: the series for sin, the real-variable versions, Euler's formula e^{ix} = cos x + i·sin x, and Euler's identity e^{iπ} = −1.
overview.proofStrategy: Each result is the corresponding Mathlib theorem, restated. cos_eq_exp/sin_eq_exp follow from Complex.two_cos/two_sin by dividing by 2 (rw + ring). cos_eq_tsum/sin_eq_tsum (and the real versions) are Mathlib's Complex.cos_eq_tsum etc., which Mathlib derives from the exponential definition. euler_formula is Complex.exp_mul_I; euler_identity is Complex.exp_pi_mul_I.
keyInsights: Mathlib defines cos/sin through the exponential, so deriving their power series IS the content of cos_eq_tsum — the OQ's requested derivation is exactly the dependency direction Mathlib uses.
The exponential definitions cos x = (e^{ix}+e^{−ix})/2 and sin x = (e^{−ix}−e^{ix})i/2 are one rearrangement away from Euler's formula e^{ix} = cos x + i·sin x.
The power series cos z = Σ (−1)ⁿ z²ⁿ/(2n)! and sin z = Σ (−1)ⁿ z²ⁿ⁺¹/(2n+1)! split the exponential series e^{iz} = Σ (iz)ⁿ/n! into even and odd parts.
Euler's identity e^{iπ} = −1 is the value at z = π of the exponential, equivalently cos π = −1 and sin π = 0.
Both the complex and real forms hold, with the real series obtained from the complex one by casting.
